notes.meaning: Human effort cannot succeed without God's help. Builders may work hard to construct a home or build up a family, and guards may stay awake to protect a city, but their labor fails if the Lord is not with them. God does not tell people to stop working, but rather teaches them to stop trusting only in their own strength.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Early church writers such as Augustine saw the house as the church, where ministers preach and watch, but only Christ builds and preserves hearts.

notes.meaning: Working long hours with frantic worry does not bring real security. People who do not trust God wear themselves out from dawn to dark, eating their daily bread with sorrow and fear. In contrast, the Lord grants His people peaceful rest, caring for them as they trust Him instead of fretting.

Children are not an accident or a burden, but a precious gift from the Lord. God gives them freely out of His kindness and grace, rather than as wages that parents have earned. Families can receive children with joy, trusting that the God who gives them will also provide for them.

Children born while parents are still young grow up to become their defenders and helpers. Just as raw wood must be carefully shaped into straight arrows, young children need patient guidance so they can be aimed toward what is good. When guided well, they become a strong support to their parents in later years.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Augustine interpreted these arrows as the apostles, who were sent out into the world by Christ to conquer hearts for God.

notes.meaning: A parent with a home full of faithful children is richly blessed. In ancient times, city gates served as public courts of law and defense against enemies. A father surrounded by loyal, upright sons would not be easily silenced, cheated, or intimidated by his accusers.

differ.view: Some evangelicals believe this passage teaches married couples to avoid all birth control and welcome as many children as God gives.
Many evangelicals believe children are always a blessing, but God gives couples the freedom to prayerfully and wisely plan the size of their family.
